elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence opens "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Garman shall...", covering both triggers.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: The insertion commits Garman only to "transition assistance for at least ninety (90) calendar days"; no six-month duration appears anywhere.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: No pricing basis is stated for the assistance; the words "then-current rates" are absent from the rendered language.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) calendar days after such expiry or termination, export and deliver to Sparkling all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Sparkling."

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: The delivery obligation specifies no format; no "commonly used, machine-readable format" language is included.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: The only certification in the document runs the other way (Section 17(b): Sparkling certifies destruction/return of Software, Documentation and Codes); no Garman deletion certification is added.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason" expressly captures both expiry and termination, for any cause.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "Garman shall, at Sparkling's request, provide transition assistance for at least ninety (90) calendar days" — a floor of 90 days, on a general request condition not limited to anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) calendar days after such expiry or termination, export and deliver to Sparkling all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Sparkling" — the 30-day clock runs from the termination/expiry event and the data scope covers all Customer data categories.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete in operative language: expiry-or-termination trigger, a 90-day floor of transition assistance, and export/delivery of all Sparkling data within 30 days of the triggering event.

Preferred level is not reached: no six-month assistance period, no "then-current rates" pricing basis, no machine-readable format requirement, and no Garman certification of deletion after return. To reach preferred, the drafter would need to extend assistance to six months at Vendor's then-current rates, require return "in a commonly used, machine-readable format", and add a post-return deletion-and-written-certification obligation.

Minimal: a single concise insertion into the termination section for a genuinely missing clause; no existing words (including the Customer-side certification in Section 17(b) and the perpetual-licence/fee-refund mechanics) were deleted or paraphrased, and no extras such as survival tails, at-own-expense language or procedures were added.

Preserves intent: the new paragraph is purely additive, uses only defined party names, creates no dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict Section 17(b)'s obligation for Sparkling to return Software, Documentation and Codes or Section 16/18 mechanics.
Finding status "missing" is corroborated: the cited paragraphs address only Sparkling's return obligations and fee refunds, with no exit assistance or return/export of Customer data.
